# x2 — Plan

**Audience:** an implementing model (deepseek-v4-flash).

Every step is self-contained and test-first: write the tests, watch them fail for the right
reason, implement, watch them pass. Do all four phases within the one step, in order, before
marking it done.


---

## 0. Read this first — how this codebase actually works

You must understand these five facts or you will write code that silently does nothing.

### 0.1 There is no SQL database. Qdrant is the primary store.

`src/lib/server/qdrant.ts` wraps a single Qdrant collection named `x2` (constant `C`). **Every**
record — users, messages, groups, folders, push subscriptions, read markers — is a point in that
one collection, discriminated by a `s` ("shape") field in the payload:

| `s` | meaning | defined in |
|-----|---------|-----------|
| `'u'` | user | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'m'` | message | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'x'` | legacy random-match record | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'sm'` | scheduled message | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'g'` | group ("room") | `src/lib/server/group.ts` |
| `'fo'` | folder | `src/lib/server/folders.ts` |
| `'ps'` | push subscription | `src/lib/server/subs.ts` |
| `'rd'` | read marker | `src/lib/server/unread.ts` |
| `'mu'` | **mute — you will add this** | `src/lib/server/mute.ts` (new) |

Query helpers: `eq(key, value)`, `range(key, gte, lte)`, `f(...conds)` (AND), `f_or(musts, anyOf)`,
then `scroll(env, filter, limit)` (non-vector list) or `search(env, vector, filter, limit)`
(vector similarity).

### 0.2 Two Qdrant rules that cause silent data loss

**Rule A — every field you filter on MUST be indexed.** The collection runs in `strict_mode`, which
*rejects* a filter naming an unindexed payload key. Indexes are declared in `ensure()`
(`src/lib/server/qdrant.ts:78-90`). If you `eq('tg', x)` without adding `tg` there, the query
errors.

**Rule B — every Qdrant write and read in this repo swallows its errors.** Look at
`upsert`/`scroll`/`search`/`remove`: they all end in `.catch(() => {})` or `.catch(() => [])`. A
rejected request therefore looks *exactly* like "nothing matched". Combined with Rule A, forgetting
an index produces a feature that appears to work in tests and does nothing in production. Double
check the index list every time you add a filter.

**Rule C — Qdrant point IDs must be an unsigned integer or a UUID.** Nothing else is accepted.
`src/lib/server/unread.ts:6` currently violates this (see §2.1) and, because of Rule B, has been
failing silently. Use `uuid_from(someDeterministicString)` (`qdrant.ts:49`) whenever you need a
deterministic, overwritable point id — that is the pattern `src/lib/server/subs.ts:20` already uses.

### 0.3 "Rooms" are `Group` records

The product word is **room**; the code word is **group**. `/app/rooms` → `src/lib/server/group.ts`,
`/api/groups`. Do **not** rename anything. A room's conversation id is `` `g:${groupId}` ``
(`group_conv_id()` in `src/lib/server/chat.ts:43`).

### 0.4 Realtime is a separate Cloudflare Worker

- `ws/` is its own worker (`x2-ws`), bound to the main worker as the `X2_WS` service binding and
  reachable in handlers as `locals.x2_ws` (`src/hooks.server.ts:31`).
- `ws/src/hub.ts` defines the `ChatHub` Durable Object — **one DO instance per user id**
  (`idFromName(uid)`). It holds that user's open WebSockets via hibernatable
  `state.acceptWebSocket(server, [uid])`.
- Send flow (`src/routes/api/send/+server.ts`): store message in Qdrant → POST `/relay` to `x2-ws` →
  `ws/src/relay.ts` fans out to each recipient's `ChatHub` → each hub reports `delivered: boolean`
  → the API pushes a Web Push notification **only to the uids reported `undelivered`**.
- Client side: `src/lib/ws.ts` is a single shared socket per tab. `ws_on(fn)` subscribes,
  `ws_send(obj, keep)` sends (`keep` = replay on every reconnect).

### 0.5 Test layout

`vite.config.ts` defines two vitest projects:
- **`node`** — `src/**/*.test.ts` + `ws/**/*.test.ts`, excluding `src/lib/components/**`.
- **`component`** — `src/lib/components/**/*.test.ts` only, jsdom, `vitest-setup-client.ts`.

Consequence: **Svelte files under `src/routes/` are currently untestable.** Work package WP0 widens
this. Existing conventions to copy:
- server-module test → mock `../qdrant` with `vi.hoisted` (see `src/lib/server/__tests__/folders.test.ts`)
- route-handler test → mock `$env/dynamic/private` and `$lib/server/*`, hand-build the event object
  (see `src/routes/api/read/__tests__/server.test.ts`)
- component-with-bindable-prop test → a `*Host.test.svelte` wrapper
  (see `src/lib/components/__tests__/ModalHost.test.svelte`)

### 0.6 Conventions you must match

- Tabs for indentation. Single quotes. Prettier config at `prettier.config.js`; run `pnpm format`.
- Svelte 5 runes only: `$props()`, `$state()`, `$derived()`, `$effect()`, `$bindable()`. No
  `export let`, no legacy stores except the existing `$page` import from `$app/stores`.
- Tailwind v4, CSS-first. Design tokens live in `@theme` in `src/app.css`. Component classes
  (`.btn`, `.card`, `.wrap`, `.eyebrow`, `.person`, `.reveal`) live in `@layer components`.
- Icons: `@lucide/svelte`, named imports only (`import { Search } from '@lucide/svelte'`).
- Copy is lowercase and terse ("find rooms", "say something to the room…"). Match it.
- Comments explain *why*, never *what*. Only write one where the reason is non-obvious.

## How tests are written in this repo

Copy these three patterns exactly. Do not invent a fourth.

### Pattern A — a server module (`src/lib/server/*.ts`)

Mock the Qdrant layer so nothing touches the network, then assert on what was *written*. From
`src/lib/server/__tests__/folders.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';

const { ensureMock, upsertMock, scrollMock, removeMock } = vi.hoisted(() => ({
    ensureMock: vi.fn(),
    upsertMock: vi.fn(),
    scrollMock: vi.fn(),
    removeMock: vi.fn()
}));

vi.mock('../qdrant', async () => {
    const actual = await vi.importActual<typeof import('../qdrant')>('../qdrant');
    return { ...actual, ensure: ensureMock, upsert: upsertMock, scroll: scrollMock, remove: removeMock };
});

import { save_folder /* … */ } from '../folders';

const ENV = { QDRANT_URL: 'u', QDRANT_KEY: 'k' };

beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    ensureMock.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
    upsertMock.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
    scrollMock.mockResolvedValue([]);
    removeMock.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
});
```

Note `importActual` — the real `eq`/`f`/`uuid_from`/`ZV` stay live so you can assert on real filter
shapes. Keep it that way.

### Pattern B — a route handler (`src/routes/**/+server.ts`)

Mock `$env/dynamic/private` and every `$lib/server/*` the handler imports, then hand-build the
event. From `src/routes/api/read/__tests__/server.test.ts`:

```ts
vi.mock('$env/dynamic/private', () => ({ env: {} }));
vi.mock('$lib/server/unread', () => ({ mark_read: markMock, unread_by_conv: byConvMock }));

import { GET, POST } from '../+server';

function event(body?: unknown, uid: string | null = 'me') {
    return {
        request: new Request('https://x/api/thing', {
            method: 'POST',
            headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
            ...(body === undefined ? {} : { body: JSON.stringify(body) })
        }),
        locals: { user: uid ? { id: uid, username: 'me' } : null }
    } as unknown as Parameters<typeof POST>[0];
}
```

Thrown SvelteKit errors are asserted with
`await expect(GET(event(…))).rejects.toMatchObject({ status: 401 })`.

### Pattern C — a Svelte component

Lives in the jsdom `component` vitest project. For a component with a `$bindable()` prop you need a
host wrapper, because `@testing-library/svelte` cannot bind directly. See
`src/lib/components/__tests__/ModalHost.test.svelte` and `SelectHost.test.svelte`.

**File-naming rule (new, introduced by WP0.C):** any test that renders a component is named
`<Thing>.svelte.test.ts`. Everything else is `<thing>.test.ts`. The vitest config routes them.

### What not to test

- Don't test that Tailwind classes are present on an element — that is asserting the implementation
  back to itself. Test *behaviour*: what renders, what a click does, what gets fetched.
  The two exceptions in this plan (the `mobile-nav-and-alignment` step) are explicitly about CSS being the product.
- Don't snapshot-test markup.
- Don't add a test for a one-line pass-through that has no branch.

## WP0 — Preflight

### 0.A `pnpm-workspace.yaml` — already fixed, do not touch

For context only. This file used to read:

```yaml
allowBuilds:
  esbuild: set this to true or false
  workerd: set this to true or false
```

Placeholder strings instead of booleans, and no `packages` key — so `pnpm test` died in its implicit
`pnpm install` with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`. It now reads:

```yaml
packages:
  - '.'
allowBuilds:
  esbuild: true
  workerd: true
```

`packages: ['.']` is required next to `allowBuilds`; without it pnpm aborts install outright. Leave
this file alone, and **do not delete it** — an earlier commit (`fedfe48`) deleted it as a workaround,
which is not the fix.

### 0.B Confirm the baseline

```bash
pnpm test
```

Expected before you change anything: **54 files, 578 tests, all passing.** If that is not what you
see, stop and report it — do not start work on a red baseline.

### 0.C Make page components testable

`src/routes/**/*.svelte` cannot be tested today. You will add real UI there (filters modal,
description modal, folder bar), so widen the vitest projects.

Edit `vite.config.ts`:

```ts
test: {
    projects: [
        {
            extends: true,
            test: {
                name: 'node',
                environment: 'node',
                include: ['src/**/*.{test,spec}.ts', 'ws/**/*.{test,spec}.ts'],
                // *.svelte.test.ts is the jsdom project's territory — these render
                // components and need a DOM, so keep them out of the node project.
                exclude: ['src/lib/components/**', 'src/**/*.svelte.{test,spec}.ts']
            }
        },
        {
            extends: true,
            resolve: { conditions: ['browser'] },
            test: {
                name: 'component',
                environment: 'jsdom',
                include: [
                    'src/lib/components/**/*.{test,spec}.ts',
                    'src/**/*.svelte.{test,spec}.ts'
                ],
                setupFiles: ['./vitest-setup-client.ts']
            }
        }
    ]
}
```

**Naming rule from here on:** any test that renders a Svelte component is named
`<Thing>.svelte.test.ts`. Everything else stays `<thing>.test.ts`.

### 0.D Prefer extraction over inline markup

Whenever a work package below adds non-trivial UI to a page, put it in
`src/lib/components/<Name>.svelte` and import it. Two reasons: the `component` vitest project
already covers that directory, and several of these widgets are needed on more than one page.

---

════════════════════════ PART 2 — TEST-SIDE WORK ════════════════════════

## T0 — Preflight

**T0.1 — the baseline is green.** Not a file; a gate. Run `pnpm test` before touching anything
and record the numbers. If they are not 54/578, stop and report.

**T0.2 — the widened vitest config actually routes files.** After editing `vite.config.ts`, add a
throwaway `src/routes/app/__tests__/smoke.svelte.test.ts` that renders any existing component and
asserts it mounted. Confirm it runs under the `component` project (`pnpm exec vitest run --project component`)
and **not** under `node`. Then delete it. This guards against the config change silently doing
nothing.

---

When both parts are done and `pnpm test` is green, commit and run `plan.ts plan preflight`.

### T1.1 — indexes cover every filter key
**File:** `src/lib/server/__tests__/qdrant.test.ts` *(new)*

This is the most valuable test in the plan. Qdrant's `strict_mode` rejects a filter on an unindexed

a user reports a feature "doing nothing".

- `it('creates a payload index for every key any module filters on')` — mock `qc()` to return a fake
  client capturing `createPayloadIndex` calls; call `ensure({…})`; assert the captured field names
  are a superset of: `s`, `t`, `r`, `c`, `f`, `co`, `st`, `ci`, `u`, `ow`, `mb`, `gr`, `uid`, `ac`,
  `tg`, `k`, `ag`, `at`, `sent`.
- `it('is idempotent — a second call does not re-issue index creation')` — the module-level `ensured`
  flag. Call twice, assert `createCollection` ran once.
- `it('does not throw when the collection already exists')` — make `createCollection` reject; assert
  `ensure` resolves.

### T1.2 — `search()` and `scroll()` forward `offset`
**File:** same

- `it('passes offset through to the Qdrant client on search')`
- `it('passes offset through to the Qdrant client on scroll')`
- `it('omits offset when not given, so existing callers are unaffected')` — assert the property is
  `undefined`, not `0`.

### T1.3 — `read_id` produces a valid Qdrant point id
**File:** `src/lib/server/__tests__/unread.test.ts` *(existing — modify)*

The current implementation returns `` `read:${uid}:${conv}` ``, which Qdrant rejects outright (point
ids must be an unsigned int or a UUID). Because `upsert` swallows the error, read markers have never
persisted and unread counts have never gone down.

**New test — this is the one that catches the live bug:**

```ts
it('returns a UUID, the only string form Qdrant accepts as a point id', async () => {
    expect(await read_id('me', 'a|b')).toMatch(
        /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/
    );
});
```

- line 23, the `read()` helper → `async`, or precompute ids in the test body
- line 45 `is stable for the same user and conversation` → `await` both sides
- line 49 `differs per user` → `await`
- line 53 `differs per conversation` → `await`

`src/lib/server/qdrant.ts` wraps a single Qdrant collection named `x2` (constant `C`). **Every**
record — users, messages, groups, folders, push subscriptions, read markers — is a point in that
one collection, discriminated by a `s` ("shape") field in the payload:

| `s` | meaning | defined in |
|-----|---------|-----------|
| `'u'` | user | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'m'` | message | `src/lib/types.ts` |

**Rule A — every field you filter on MUST be indexed.** The collection runs in `strict_mode`, which

errors.

**Rule B — every Qdrant write and read in this repo swallows its errors.** Look at
`upsert`/`scroll`/`search`/`remove`: they all end in `.catch(() => {})` or `.catch(() => [])`. A
rejected request therefore looks *exactly* like "nothing matched". Combined with Rule A, forgetting
an index produces a feature that appears to work in tests and does nothing in production. Double
check the index list every time you add a filter.

**Rule C — Qdrant point IDs must be an unsigned integer or a UUID.** Nothing else is accepted.
`src/lib/server/unread.ts:6` currently violates this (see §2.1) and, because of Rule B, has been
failing silently. Use `uuid_from(someDeterministicString)` (`qdrant.ts:49`) whenever you need a

## WP2 — Muting a room or a user

### 2.1 Design decisions (do not deviate)

**A mute suppresses *notification*, never *delivery*.** A muted conversation still relays over the
WebSocket, still appends to the open thread, still increments its per-conversation unread count. It
does not fire a Web Push and does not contribute to the app-icon badge. This mirrors WhatsApp and
is what users expect.

**Mutes are keyed by target, not by conversation id.** The codebase has two different "conversation
key" spaces already — `Folder.convs` stores a bare peer uid, while `unread`/`Read.c` stores
`conv_id(a,b)` (`"a|b"` sorted) — and conflating them is the easiest bug to write here. Sidestep it:
a mute stores the *target* (a peer uid, or a room id) plus a kind. At every enforcement point you
already have both the viewer and the target in hand.

**A mute may expire.** `until: 0` means indefinite; otherwise a unix-ms timestamp. Expiry is
evaluated on read (`until === 0 || until > Date.now()`); no cleanup job. Offer 8 hours, 1 week, and
forever in the UI.

### 2.2 New file `src/lib/server/mute.ts`

```ts
import { ensure, upsert, scroll, remove, uuid_from, f, eq, ZV, type QEnv } from './qdrant';

export interface Mute {
    s: 'mu';
    ow: string;    // uid of the person who muted (indexed: 'ow')
    tg: string;    // target — peer uid for 'u', room id for 'r' (indexed: 'tg')
    k: 'u' | 'r';  // kind (indexed: 'k')
    until: number; // 0 = indefinite, else unix ms when the mute lapses
    d: number;     // created ts
}

// deterministic id: re-muting the same target overwrites rather than duplicating, and
// unmute is a delete of the same id — no read-then-delete round trip
const mute_id = (owner: string, target: string) => uuid_from(`mute:${owner}:${target}`);

export const is_active = (m: Mute, now = Date.now()): boolean => m.until === 0 || m.until > now;

export async function mute(
    env: QEnv,
    owner: string,
    target: string,
    kind: 'u' | 'r',
    until = 0
): Promise<Mute> {
    await ensure(env);
    const m: Mute = { s: 'mu', ow: owner, tg: target, k: kind, until, d: Date.now() };
    await upsert(env, [
        { id: await mute_id(owner, target), vector: ZV, payload: m as unknown as Record<string, unknown> }
    ]);
    return m;
}

export async function unmute(env: QEnv, owner: string, target: string): Promise<void> {
    await ensure(env);
    await remove(env, [await mute_id(owner, target)]);
}

/** every live mute this user owns */
export async function list_mutes(env: QEnv, owner: string, now = Date.now()): Promise<Mute[]> {
    await ensure(env);
    const pts = await scroll(env, f(eq('s', 'mu'), eq('ow', owner)), 500);
    return pts.map((p) => p.payload as unknown as Mute).filter((m) => is_active(m, now));
}

/** has `owner` muted `target`? */
export async function is_muted(
    env: QEnv,
    owner: string,
    target: string,
    now = Date.now()
): Promise<boolean> {
    await ensure(env);
    const pts = await scroll(env, f(eq('s', 'mu'), eq('ow', owner), eq('tg', target)), 1);
    const m = pts[0]?.payload as unknown as Mute | undefined;
    return !!m && is_active(m, now);
}

/**
 * Which of `uids` have muted `target`. One query for the whole room instead of one per
 * member — a 50-person room fanning out 50 scrolls would blow the subrequest budget.
 */
export async function muters_of(
    env: QEnv,
    target: string,
    uids: string[],
    now = Date.now()
): Promise<Set<string>> {
    if (!uids.length) return new Set();
    await ensure(env);
    const pts = await scroll(env, f(eq('s', 'mu'), eq('tg', target)), 1000);
    const candidates = new Set(uids);
    return new Set(
        pts
            .map((p) => p.payload as unknown as Mute)
            .filter((m) => is_active(m, now) && candidates.has(m.ow))
            .map((m) => m.ow)
    );
}

/** drop the uids that muted `target` — the shape every notify() call site needs */
export async function drop_muted(
    env: QEnv,
    target: string,
    uids: string[],
    now = Date.now()
): Promise<string[]> {
    const muted = await muters_of(env, target, uids, now);
    return uids.filter((u) => !muted.has(u));
}
```

## 0. Read this first — how this codebase actually works

### 0.1 There is no SQL database. Qdrant is the primary store.

`src/lib/server/qdrant.ts` wraps a single Qdrant collection named `x2` (constant `C`). **Every**
record — users, messages, groups, folders, push subscriptions, read markers — is a point in that
one collection, discriminated by a `s` ("shape") field in the payload:

| `s` | meaning | defined in |
|-----|---------|-----------|
| `'u'` | user | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'m'` | message | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'x'` | legacy random-match record | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'sm'` | scheduled message | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'g'` | group ("room") | `src/lib/server/group.ts` |
| `'fo'` | folder | `src/lib/server/folders.ts` |
| `'ps'` | push subscription | `src/lib/server/subs.ts` |
| `'rd'` | read marker | `src/lib/server/unread.ts` |
| `'mu'` | **mute — you will add this** | `src/lib/server/mute.ts` (new) |

then `scroll(env, filter, limit)` (non-vector list) or `search(env, vector, filter, limit)`
(vector similarity).

### 0.2 Two Qdrant rules that cause silent data loss

**Rule A — every field you filter on MUST be indexed.** The collection runs in `strict_mode`, which
*rejects* a filter naming an unindexed payload key. Indexes are declared in `ensure()`
(`src/lib/server/qdrant.ts:78-90`). If you `eq('tg', x)` without adding `tg` there, the query
errors.

**Rule B — every Qdrant write and read in this repo swallows its errors.** Look at
`upsert`/`scroll`/`search`/`remove`: they all end in `.catch(() => {})` or `.catch(() => [])`. A
rejected request therefore looks *exactly* like "nothing matched". Combined with Rule A, forgetting
an index produces a feature that appears to work in tests and does nothing in production. Double
check the index list every time you add a filter.

**Rule C — Qdrant point IDs must be an unsigned integer or a UUID.** Nothing else is accepted.
`src/lib/server/unread.ts:6` currently violates this (see §2.1) and, because of Rule B, has been
failing silently. Use `uuid_from(someDeterministicString)` (`qdrant.ts:49`) whenever you need a

```ts
// The server uses this to decide whether a live socket counts as "the user saw it".
// A backgrounded PWA keeps its socket open, so without this every push is suppressed.
function report_active(): void {
    if (typeof document === 'undefined') return;
    const on = document.visibilityState === 'visible';
    // `keep` so the state is re-sent on every reconnect — a socket that reconnects while
    // hidden must not come back marked active.
    ws_send({ type: 'active', on }, true);
```

would both accumulate in the handshake queue. Use `ws_drop` to remove the opposite variant before

```ts
ws_drop({ type: 'active', on: !on });
ws_send({ type: 'active', on }, true);
```

```ts
private deliver(uid: string, payload: unknown): boolean {
    const data = JSON.stringify(payload);
    const sockets = this.state.getWebSockets(uid);
    let seen = false;
    for (const ws of sockets) {
        try {
            ws.send(data);
            // A socket that never reported its state is assumed active — old clients
            // must keep working, and over-reporting delivery is the pre-existing
            // behaviour, not a regression.
            const att = ws.deserializeAttachment() as { active?: boolean } | null;
            if (att?.active !== false) seen = true;
        } catch {
            try { ws.close(1011, 'delivery failed'); } catch {}
        }
    }
```

## 0. Read this first — how this codebase actually works

You must understand these five facts or you will write code that silently does nothing.

### 0.1 There is no SQL database. Qdrant is the primary store.

`src/lib/server/qdrant.ts` wraps a single Qdrant collection named `x2` (constant `C`). **Every**
record — users, messages, groups, folders, push subscriptions, read markers — is a point in that
one collection, discriminated by a `s` ("shape") field in the payload:

| `s` | meaning | defined in |
|-----|---------|-----------|
| `'u'` | user | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'m'` | message | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'x'` | legacy random-match record | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'sm'` | scheduled message | `src/lib/types.ts` |
| `'g'` | group ("room") | `src/lib/server/group.ts` |
| `'fo'` | folder | `src/lib/server/folders.ts` |
| `'ps'` | push subscription | `src/lib/server/subs.ts` |
| `'rd'` | read marker | `src/lib/server/unread.ts` |
| `'mu'` | **mute — you will add this** | `src/lib/server/mute.ts` (new) |

Query helpers: `eq(key, value)`, `range(key, gte, lte)`, `f(...conds)` (AND), `f_or(musts, anyOf)`,
then `scroll(env, filter, limit)` (non-vector list) or `search(env, vector, filter, limit)`
(vector similarity).

### 0.2 Two Qdrant rules that cause silent data loss

**Rule A — every field you filter on MUST be indexed.** The collection runs in `strict_mode`, which
*rejects* a filter naming an unindexed payload key. Indexes are declared in `ensure()`
(`src/lib/server/qdrant.ts:78-90`). If you `eq('tg', x)` without adding `tg` there, the query
errors.

**Rule B — every Qdrant write and read in this repo swallows its errors.** Look at
`upsert`/`scroll`/`search`/`remove`: they all end in `.catch(() => {})` or `.catch(() => [])`. A
rejected request therefore looks *exactly* like "nothing matched". Combined with Rule A, forgetting
an index produces a feature that appears to work in tests and does nothing in production. Double
check the index list every time you add a filter.

**Rule C — Qdrant point IDs must be an unsigned integer or a UUID.** Nothing else is accepted.
`src/lib/server/unread.ts:6` currently violates this (see §2.1) and, because of Rule B, has been
failing silently. Use `uuid_from(someDeterministicString)` (`qdrant.ts:49`) whenever you need a
deterministic, overwritable point id — that is the pattern `src/lib/server/subs.ts:20` already uses.

### 0.3 "Rooms" are `Group` records

The product word is **room**; the code word is **group**. `/app/rooms` → `src/lib/server/group.ts`,
`/api/groups`. Do **not** rename anything. A room's conversation id is `` `g:${groupId}` ``
(`group_conv_id()` in `src/lib/server/chat.ts:43`).

### 0.4 Realtime is a separate Cloudflare Worker

- `ws/` is its own worker (`x2-ws`), bound to the main worker as the `X2_WS` service binding and
  reachable in handlers as `locals.x2_ws` (`src/hooks.server.ts:31`).
- `ws/src/hub.ts` defines the `ChatHub` Durable Object — **one DO instance per user id**

  `state.acceptWebSocket(server, [uid])`.
- Send flow (`src/routes/api/send/+server.ts`): store message in Qdrant → POST `/relay` to `x2-ws` →

- Client side: `src/lib/ws.ts` is a single shared socket per tab. `ws_on(fn)` subscribes,
  `ws_send(obj, keep)` sends (`keep` = replay on every reconnect).
